title: On which item does the family spend the most and the second most?
description: The bar graph of a family's monthly spending is read to find the tallest and the second tallest bars. The two amounts are then checked against the scale of two hundred rupees for one unit, and Keeko's doubt, that the first bar must be the largest, is checked against the heights.
teaching_notes: One idea: the tallest bar is the most and the next tallest is the second most, wherever they stand in the row. Watch for students who pick the first bar.

source: Using Laksh's family bar graph (House rent 3000, Food 3400, Education 800, Electricity 400, Transport 600, Miscellaneous 1200): On which item does Laksh's family spend the most and the second most?
video_script.why: The child reads a finished bar graph to find the tallest and the second tallest bars, and says what they stand for.
video_script.substitution: Compare the heights of all six bars, pick the tallest and the next tallest, and read their amounts with the scale.
video_script.anchor: the bar graph of the monthly spending of the family, with six bars and the scale 1 unit length = Rs 200
video_script.wrong_answer: house rent is the most, because its bar comes first
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko picks the first bar in the row. The place of a bar does not matter, only its height.
video_script.payoff_line: The most is spent on food and the second most on house rent

final_answer.value: most on food (3400), second most on house rent (3000)
final_answer.spoken: the most is spent on food and the second most on house rent

names.Laksh: boy whose family's monthly spending is shown in the bar graph

maths_rules: bar heights in units: house rent 15, food 17, education 4, electricity 2, transport 3, miscellaneous 1200 / 200 = 6
tallest bar: food, 17 units, 17 x 200 = 3400 rupees
second tallest bar: house rent, 15 units, 15 x 200 = 3000 rupees
video_script.design: One idea: compare the heights, tallest is most and next tallest is second most, whatever the order in the row. The finished bar graph stays on the board all video.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the finished bar graph of the monthly spending of the family, six bars, with the scale 1 unit length = Rs 200

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.graph: the finished bar graph of the six items appears
marks.ask: a question mark appears over the bars

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about Laksh's family.
<bookmark mark='graph'/>Their monthly spending on six things is shown as bars.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>On which item do they spend the most, and on which the second most?

beats.on_screen: the graph stays on the board and Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: two bars side by side, a taller one labelled more money and a shorter one labelled less money; the label 1 unit length = Rs 200

marks.two: two bars stand side by side, one taller than the other
marks.more: the taller bar is labelled more money and the shorter bar less money
marks.scale: the label 1 unit length = Rs 200 appears

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>In a bar graph, we compare the heights of the bars.
<bookmark mark='more'/>A taller bar stands for more money, and a shorter bar for less money.
<bookmark mark='scale'/>Every bar uses the same scale, so heights are fair to compare.

beats.on_screen: Given: bar heights in units: House rent 15, Food 17, Education 4, Electricity 2, Transport 3, Miscellaneous 6; 1 unit length = Rs 200

marks.first: the heights 15, 17 and 4 are written above the first three bars
marks.last: the heights 2, 3 and 6 are written above the last three bars

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Given, the first three bars are fifteen, seventeen and four units tall.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last three are two, three and six units tall.

beats.on_screen: To find: the tallest bar and the second tallest bar

marks.find: the words the tallest bar and the second tallest bar are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the tallest bar and the second tallest bar.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the tallest bar is the second bar, 17 units; the other heights 15, 4, 2, 3, 6 are all smaller

marks.scan: a line is run across the tops of all six bars
marks.top: the second bar, 17 units, is lit as the tallest

narration: <bookmark mark='scan'/>Step one, run your eye along the tops of all six bars.
<bookmark mark='top'/>The second bar reaches seventeen units. Every other bar is shorter, so it is the tallest.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: leave out the tallest bar; the next tallest is the first bar, 15 units, and 15 > 6 > 4 > 3 > 2

marks.next: the first bar, 15 units, is lit as the next tallest

narration: <bookmark mark='cover'/>Step two, cover the tallest bar and look again at the rest.
<bookmark mark='next'/>The first bar is fifteen units, and the others are six or less. That makes it the second tallest.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: read the money with the scale. 17 x 200 = 3400; 15 x 200 = 3000

marks.big: 17 x 200 = 3400 is written beside the tallest bar
marks.next: 15 x 200 = 3000 is written beside the next bar

narration: <bookmark mark='big'/>Step three, read the money with the scale. Seventeen times two hundred is three thousand four hundred rupees.
<bookmark mark='next'/>Fifteen times two hundred is three thousand rupees.

beats.on_screen: Answer: most on food (3400), second most on house rent (3000)

marks.pay: the answer line is boxed and the two bars are shaded

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>The most is spent on food and the second most on house rent.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the bar graph
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble says house rent is the most because its bar comes first; the bubble is struck through; the bars are put in order of height

marks.place: an arrow shows that the first place in the row means nothing
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the bars are sorted by height

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks house rent is the most, because its bar comes first.
<bookmark mark='place'/>But the place of a bar in the row tells us nothing. Only its height counts.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Sort the bars by height, and the second bar moves ahead of the first.
